topic: Dockerizing Java and Spring Boot Applications
learningObjectives: Explain how containers package Java applications with their runtime requirements.
Identify the major instructions in a Java Dockerfile.
Construct a containerization workflow for a Spring Boot application.

activities.title: Container Architecture
activities.instruction: Explore the main parts of a containerized Java application.

content.concept: A container runs an application in an isolated environment created from an image. The image contains the application and the runtime components needed by the application.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The Spring Boot application that will run inside the container.
Instructions describing how to build the application image.
A packaged, immutable template used to create containers.
A running instance created from an image.
A service used to store and distribute container images.

activities.title: Dockerfile Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the important instructions in a Java Dockerfile.

content.concept: A Java Dockerfile commonly selects a base runtime image, copies the application artifact, defines a working directory when needed, documents the application port, and specifies how the application starts.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Selects the base image for the container.
Sets the working directory for subsequent instructions.
Copies files from the build context into the image.
Documents the port the application is expected to use.
Defines the default command used to start the container.

activities.title: Containerization Workflow
activities.instruction: Arrange the main steps for containerizing a Spring Boot application.

content.concept: A typical workflow packages the application, builds an image from the Dockerfile, starts a container, and verifies that the application is accessible.
